editorial_note: Canto 11 data remains under full source and translation review. The Sanskrit and English records are draft material tied to the pinned source; phrase coverage and all lexical choices still require chapter-by-chapter verification.

entries.sanskrit: ईश्वरेच्छयोत्थितं ब्रह्म-शाप-निमित्तं वक्तुम् आह---कर्माणीति । कर्मार्थम् आहूताः कर्माणि कृत्व निसृष्टा मुनयः पिण्डारकं समगमन्न् इत्य् अन्वयः । निसृष्टाः प्रस्थापिताः पूर्वोक्ताम् उदार-कीर्तितां विवृण्वन् कर्माणि विशिनष्टि---पुण्य-निवहानि इत्य्-आदि त्रिभिः पदैः । कानिचिद् अश्वमेधादि-कर्माणि पुण्यम् एव जनयन्ति । पुत्रोपलालनादीनि तु तत्-काले सुखम् एव कुर्वन्ति । प्रायश्चित्तादीनि तु पापम् एव हरन्ति । एतानि तु सर्वतो-मुखानीत्य् आह पुण्य-निवहानि । कीर्तनादिन पुण्यानि निवहन्ति प्रापयन्तीति । तथा सुमङ्गलान्य् अतिसुखात्मकानि । गायतो जगतः कलि-मलापहराणि कृत्वा । मुनि-प्रस्थापने हेतुः---कालात्मना संहारक-रूपेण यदु-देव-गेहे वसुदेव-गृहे निवसता स्व-कुलं सञ्जिहीर्षतेत्य् अर्थः । पीण्डारकं ततो नातिदूरं तीर्थ-विशेषम् ॥११॥
word_for_word: the occasion of the brahmins' curse
he says in order to tell it
summoned for the sake of rites
the sages, having been sent off
with the three expressions beginning 'bringing abundant merit'
some rites, such as the horse sacrifice
but such things as nurturing children
bring pleasure only at the time
these, however, work in every direction
through singing their praise and similar acts
they bring forth, that is, confer merits
of the world that sings [of them]
the reason for sending the sages away
in the house of the lord of the Yadus
wishing to withdraw his own dynasty
entries.literal_english: To explain how the occasion for the brahmins' curse arose through the Lord's will, he begins 'acts.' The construction is: the sages, summoned to perform rites, performed them and, when sent off, went to Piṇḍāraka. 'Sent off' means dispatched. Expanding on the previously stated 'generous fame,' he qualifies the acts with three expressions beginning 'bringing abundant merit.' Some acts, such as horse sacrifices, generate merit alone; nurturing children and the like produce pleasure at that time alone; expiations remove sin alone. These acts, however, accomplish all these ends: through their glorification they bestow merits, are exceptionally auspicious and full of great happiness, and remove Kali's impurity from the world that sings of them. The reason the sages were dispatched was that the Lord, residing in Vasudeva's house as Time in its destructive form, wished to withdraw his dynasty. Piṇḍāraka is a particular sacred place not very far away.
entries.note: The source writes both पिण्डारकं and पीण्डारकं; both are preserved within their respective commentary locations. The final interpretation of कालात्मना belongs to Śrīdhara.

entries.attribution: Jointly labelled Śrīdhara Svāmī and Viśvanātha Cakravartī in this witness
entries.literal_english: 'Having respectfully grasped' means having taken hold of their feet.
entries.note: This brief gloss is printed under a joint Śrīdhara–Viśvanātha label; it cannot be certified as a uniquely Śrīdhara reading from this witness alone. The source has no separate commentary on verse 12.

entries.sanskrit: प्रश्न-प्रकारम् आह---ते वेषयित्वेति द्वयेन । हे अमोघ-दर्शना विप्राः ! एषा अन्तर्वत्नी गर्भिणी ॥ वो युष्मान् साक्षात् प्रष्टुं विलज्जती लज्जमानास्मन्-मुखेन पृच्छति । प्रसोष्यन्ती आसन्न-प्रसवा । किं स्वित् सञ्जनयिष्यति ? कन्यां वा पुत्रं वा, तत् प्रब्रूत ॥१४-१५॥
word_for_word: he states the form of the question
in the two verses beginning 'they disguised'
O brahmins whose vision is unfailing
what indeed will she bring forth?
entries.literal_english: He explains the form of their question in the two verses beginning 'they disguised.' 'O brahmins whose vision is unfailing! This woman is pregnant. Too embarrassed to ask you directly, she asks through us. She is about to give birth. What will she produce, a daughter or a son? Tell us.'
entries.note: The two verses receive one shared Śrīdhara explanation; the two verse numbers are not expanded into invented separate comments.

entries.literal_english: 'In that' means 'in the belly'; 'made of iron' means 'consisting of iron.'

entries.sanskrit: मन्द-भाग्यैर् नोऽस्माभिः किम् एतत् कृतम् । नोऽस्मान् किं वदिष्यतीति विह्वलिताः सन्तो मुसलम् आदाय गेहान् ययुः ॥१८॥
word_for_word: what is this that has been done?
entries.literal_english: 'What is this that we unfortunate ones have done? What will [people] say about us?' Thus distraught, they took the club and went home.
entries.note: The wording of the last question is elliptical in the pinned Sanskrit; the implied 'people' comes from the verse, not an additional Sanskrit word in Śrīdhara's comment.

entries.literal_english: 'To the king' means to Ugrasena, not to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

entries.sanskrit: आहुक उग्रसेनः । सोऽपि श्री-कृष्णम् अपृष्ट्वैव प्रास्यत् प्रक्षिप्तवान् । अस्य मुसलस्य चूर्णी-क्रियमाणस्य अवशेषितं लोहं च प्रास्यत् ॥२१॥
word_for_word: as it was being ground into powder
entries.literal_english: 'Āhuka' is Ugrasena. He too threw it away without asking Śrī Kṛṣṇa; 'threw' means 'cast away.' He also threw away the iron remaining after the club was being ground to powder.

entries.attribution: Jointly labelled Śrīdhara Svāmī and Viśvanātha Cakravartī in this witness
entries.note: Joint attribution is preserved; this witness does not independently establish the gloss as exclusive to Śrīdhara.

word_for_word: on the tip of an arrow
entries.literal_english: 'Along with others' means along with other fish; 'on the point' means on an arrowhead.

entries.sanskrit: ज्ञाताः सर्वेऽर्था येन स ईश्वरोऽपि समर्थोऽपि सन्न् अन्यथा कर्तुं नैच्छत्, किन्त्व् अन्वमोदत, यतः काल-रूपी ॥२४॥
word_for_word: by whom all matters are known
even though he is the Lord
he has the form of Time
entries.literal_english: He is one to whom all matters are known. Though the Lord and fully capable of making things otherwise, he did not wish to do so; rather, he assented, because he was in the form of Time.

scope: Complete source-bound Śrīdhara commentary for Canto 11 Chapter 1, verses 11.1.11–11.1.24; 11.1.20 has no separate commentary.
